title: Dedicated throughput SLO + tiers — Open questions & decisions log (living)
body:
Purpose
- Keep a single living log of (a) open questions that still need a decision, (b) decisions made, and (c) follow-up actions + owners.
- This doc is the working source-of-truth during the 6–8 week “Dedicated throughput SLO + tier definitions” project; finalized outcomes should be reflected in Confluence (PRD + ADRs + SLO definition + tier definition page).

How to use
- Add new items at the top under Open Questions (OQ-###).
- When decided, move item to Decisions (D-###) and add the decision date + link to ADR/Confluence if applicable.
- Keep follow-ups actionable (owner + due date + artifact).

Last updated: 2025-03-05 (post internal beta announcement)

========================================
OPEN QUESTIONS (needs decision)
========================================

OQ-019 — Tier thresholds (tokens/sec numbers) finalization + safety factor
Status: OPEN (needs final sign-off)
Context: Benchmark baselines by shape/model show variance by context length distribution + streaming patterns. Need final numbers that are (a) competitive, (b) enforceable, (c) protect error budgets.
Leading proposal:
- Use baseline p50 sustained throughput (effective output tokens/sec) with a safety factor (e.g., 0.75–0.85) depending on model class.
Owners: Lauren Bishop (decision), Irene Choi (fleet feasibility), Omar El-Sayed (runtime perf)
Due: 2025-03-08
Links: Confluence shape-to-throughput-benchmark-baselines; Drive dedicated-shapes-benchmark-results-sheet

OQ-018 — Multi-model Dedicated deployments: how SLO applies when customer pins multiple models
Status: OPEN
Question: Do we define SLO at (deployment_id, model) granularity or just deployment aggregate? If customer runs 2 models, can we guarantee per-model throughput?
Current leaning: SLO applies per deployment_id + model_version for “pinned routes”; if customers dynamically select from many models, SLO is “best effort” unless explicitly contracted.
Owners: Noah Patel, Mina Haddad, Rafael Mendes
Due: 2025-03-12

OQ-017 — Max context length cap per tier (contract + enforcement)
Status: OPEN
Question: Tiers define a reference workload envelope. Do we (a) set a hard max context per tier, (b) allow but exclude from SLO measurement, or (c) allow with throttling?
Tradeoffs: hard cap simplifies enforcement but breaks some customer use cases; exclusion is clearer but can surprise customers.
Owners: Lauren Bishop + Michael Grant
Due: 2025-03-11

OQ-016 — Streaming semantics: when does “request duration” start/end for SLI computation?
Status: OPEN
Question: For streaming responses, do we use time from request received → last token, or first token → last token (decode phase)?
Risk: If we exclude time-to-first-token (TTFT), customers may feel “throughput guarantee” doesn’t match experience.
Owners: Logan Wright (telemetry), Sofia Ivanova (runtime), Aisha Bello (SLO governance)
Due: 2025-03-07

OQ-015 — Overload behavior and customer messaging: do we prefer throttling (429) vs queueing for Standard?
Status: OPEN
Question: During overload, should Standard prioritize stable latency (throttle early) or absorb via queueing (risk tail latency)?
Leaning: throttle early for Standard to avoid runaway queues + confusing tail behavior; ensure Retry-After and clear docs.
Owners: Sofia Ivanova, Keiko Yamamoto, Owen Phillips
Due: 2025-03-10

OQ-014 — Regional availability commitments for Premium
Status: OPEN
Context: GPU supply volatility, especially H100 class. Sales wants clarity on which regions are “generally available” vs “subject to confirmation.”
Decision needed: publish a conservative region list + an exceptions process, or keep region availability entirely quote-based.
Owners: Vanessa Ortiz + Jordan Blake
Due: 2025-03-06

OQ-013 — MIG usage policy: allowed in Standard? explicitly disallowed in Premium?
Status: OPEN
Context: MIG improves packing but complicates “dedicated” story and can create noisy-neighbor within a node if not strictly isolated.
Leaning: Standard may use MIG-backed shapes (explicitly labeled); Premium = no-MIG.
Owners: Irene Choi, Sean Gallagher
Due: 2025-03-08

OQ-012 — Customer-visible exports: exact metric set and refresh cadence
Status: OPEN
Question: What do customers get by default: (a) dashboard view only, (b) CSV export, (c) API endpoint, (d) push to S3/GCS?
Leaning: CSV export + metrics API (read-only) in Performance/Premium; Standard gets dashboard view.
Owners: Chloe Martin (console), Logan Wright (telemetry), Lauren Bishop
Due: 2025-03-15

OQ-011 — Remedies/credits structure alignment with Finance
Status: OPEN
Question: If monthly throughput SLO misses, what are credits (percentage, cap), and is it tier-dependent?
Owners: Laura Bennett, Rishi Malhotra, Michael Grant
Due: 2025-03-14

========================================
DECISIONS (decided / ratified)
========================================

D-008 — Primary throughput SLO metric = sustained effective output tokens/sec (deployment-level) over rolling window
Date decided: 2025-01-23
Decision:
- Primary SLI for Dedicated throughput is “sustained effective output tokens/sec” computed per deployment_id over a rolling 5-minute window.
- Secondary metrics used as guardrails (not primary objective): TTFT p95, end-to-end latency p95 (where applicable), throttling rate, queue depth/saturation.
Notes:
- Objective is expressed as a minimum sustained throughput for admitted traffic under the tier’s reference workload envelope.
- Req/sec is supported for customer reporting but not the primary SLO.
Owner: Aisha Bello (ratification), Rafael Mendes
Links: ADR-0127; #eng-sre thread 2025-01-22

D-007 — What counts in the SLI numerator/denominator (initial v1)
Date decided: 2025-01-28
Decision (v1):
- Count only successful completions (2xx) for output tokens.
- Exclude tokens from requests that fail due to customer-induced errors (4xx except 429) or explicit customer cancellation.
- For v1, compute throughput as: sum(output_tokens) / wall_clock_seconds across the 5-minute window, where wall_clock_seconds is measured as time between request_accept and request_end aggregated across requests (i.e., accounts for concurrency).
- Maintain separate “decode-only tokens/sec” debug metric for runtime investigation.
Rationale: customer-facing metric should align with “how many tokens we actually produced for you”; concurrency-aware denominator prevents gaming by tiny requests.
Owner: Logan Wright
Follow-up: revisit streaming duration semantics (see OQ-016)
Links: throughput-measurement-standard (draft section), ENG-2194

D-006 — Maintenance window and warmup exclusions
Date decided: 2025-02-01
Decision:
- Planned maintenance windows are excluded from SLO measurement when communicated per policy.
- Warmup after scale-up/rollouts: first 10 minutes after a capacity event is excluded from SLO breach accounting, but still visible in dashboards.
Owner: Sean Gallagher
Links: dedicated-throughput-slo-definition (draft), oncall runbook skeleton

D-005 — Tier names and positioning
Date decided: 2025-01-20
Decision:
- Tier naming: Standard / Performance / Premium.
- Positioning intent:
  - Standard: cost-efficient dedicated capacity with clear throttling under overload.
  - Performance: higher sustained throughput + better burst + stronger reporting.
  - Premium: highest throughput, stricter isolation (no-MIG), priority support/operational controls.
Owner: Lauren Bishop
Links: PRD draft; #product thread 2025-01-14

D-004 — Burst policy semantics: burst is “opportunistic,” not guaranteed; throttling is expected behavior (not an SLO breach)
Date decided: 2025-02-04
Decision:
- Burst is allowed within defined ceilings and timeboxes, but is explicitly not part of the guaranteed sustained throughput.
- When burst capacity is unavailable, the platform may throttle new requests to preserve the sustained guarantee for admitted traffic.
- “Expected throttling” (429 with Retry-After) during customer load above contracted sustained levels is not an SLO breach.
Owner: Mina Haddad + Rafael Mendes
Links: ADR-0128; ENG-2206; support FAQ draft notes

D-003 — Overload mode priority: protect in-flight requests; shed/slow new admissions first
Date decided: 2025-02-07
Decision:
- Overload mode behavior (tier-dependent thresholds):
  - Do not terminate in-flight generation to regain throughput.
  - Apply admission control to new requests (rate limit + queue cap) and return 429 with Retry-After.
  - Prefer deterministic throttling over unbounded queue growth.
- Premium may allow slightly deeper queue/burst before throttling to reduce customer-visible 429s, but still has a hard cap.
Owner: Sofia Ivanova
Links: ENG-2206; PR redwood/pr-18457; #eng-runtime thread 2025-01-24

D-002 — Dashboard requirements and routing
Date decided: 2025-02-10
Decision:
- Required customer-visible panels: sustained tokens/sec vs guarantee, throttling rate, saturation/queue depth, error rate split by class (customer vs platform), and time-to-first-token p95.
- Required internal panels: shape-level GPU utilization, scheduler queue depth (prefill vs decode), cache hit rates (if enabled), and “effective tokens/sec” decomposition.
- Alerts route to Dedicated oncall (SRE) with secondary paging to Infra/Runtime based on saturation signatures.
Owner: Sergio Costa + Aisha Bello
Links: ENG-2201; observability-pack/pr-611; #eng-platform thread 2025-02-03

D-001 — Control plane must store tier and shape mapping as first-class config
Date decided: 2025-02-12
Decision:
- Tier is a first-class field on Dedicated deployments (immutable without a controlled change).
- Control plane validates region/shape/tier compatibility at provisioning time.
Owner: Ethan Park
Links: ENG-2210; redwood-terraform/pr-412

========================================
FOLLOW-UPS (action list)
========================================

FA-032 — Finalize SLO windowing + streaming duration semantics
Owner: Logan Wright
Due: 2025-03-07
Output: update throughput-measurement-standard + telemetry spec; align with ENG-2194 implementation details

FA-031 — Update Contract language draft to reflect “expected throttling is not a breach” and clear exclusions
Owner: Sofia Mendes (Commercial counsel)
Due: 2025-03-13
Output: Confluence contract language page + approved snippet for order forms

FA-030 — Publish “tier workload envelope” appendix (context length distribution assumptions)
Owner: Kira Thompson
Due: 2025-03-12
Output: Confluence tier definitions page + FAQ; include examples (mixed prompt sizes, streaming vs non-streaming)

FA-029 — Define exceptions process (requests for higher guarantees / non-standard regions)
Owner: Jordan Blake
Due: 2025-03-06
Output: sales enablement cheat sheet section + internal approval flow (who signs off)

FA-028 — Tie metrics to customer export format (CSV schema + retention)
Owner: Chloe Martin
Due: 2025-03-15
Output: console export spec + minimal UI links; coordinate with DES-144

FA-027 — Error budget simulation: choose alert thresholds for throughput SLO
Owner: Rafael Mendes
Due: 2025-03-10
Output: updated thresholds in SLO definition + alert rule PR notes; reference simulation sheet

FA-026 — Shape availability statement for Premium (by region) + “subject to confirmation” language
Owner: Vanessa Ortiz
Due: 2025-03-06
Output: tier definitions table updated + Sales FAQ entry

FA-025 — Confirm MIG policy by tier and reflect in shape catalog
Owner: Irene Choi
Due: 2025-03-08
Output: Confluence shape catalog update + control-plane validation notes

========================================
NOTES / PARKING LOT
========================================
- We keep hearing “req/sec” from search-style customers. For now we keep req/sec as a reporting view, but all guarantees are anchored in tokens/sec to avoid punishing long outputs vs short outputs.
- We should be explicit in docs that customers can increase sustained throughput by (a) moving to a bigger shape, (b) reducing max output tokens, (c) enabling caching where applicable, and (d) using batching-friendly client behavior.
- Risk: sales proposals that quote “peak” instead of “sustained.” Enablement needs to emphasize sustained vs burst.

Change log (quick)
- 2025-03-05: moved post-beta notes in; added OQ-019/OQ-018; clarified follow-ups for contract + streaming semantics.
- 2025-02-12: added D-001 control plane tier mapping decision.
- 2025-02-04: added D-004 burst policy semantics decision.
- 2025-01-23: added D-008 primary metric decision (ADR-0127).
